name: Zip Promotion Lab
purpose: Turn useful archive material into reviewed UX Apps features without importing cache, local metadata, or unrelated framework output.

lanes.label: Design System Governance
lanes.importStrategy: Adapt summary cards, token parity language, and reusable UI discipline into data-backed static sections.
lanes.value: Makes the repo feel more like a professional UX product system instead of a static catalog.
lanes.nextAction: Promote design signals into a small design system board.

lanes.label: Quality Lab
lanes.importStrategy: Convert performance, accessibility, and content governance groups into lightweight local quality cards.
lanes.value: Keeps UI expansion connected to measurable health checks.
lanes.nextAction: Add quality score rows to the full-stack surface and API.

lanes.label: Accessibility Command
lanes.importStrategy: Use the keyboard, motion, contrast, and tap-safety concepts as a review checklist.
lanes.value: Protects premium visuals from becoming inaccessible.
lanes.nextAction: Add accessibility checks to the promotion readiness model.

lanes.label: Branch Maturity System
lanes.importStrategy: Keep the domain list and non-goals as governance metadata instead of copying scripts.
lanes.value: Separates foundation, runtime, and experience growth into explainable domains.
lanes.nextAction: Introduce a maturity matrix after promotion lab usage is stable.

lanes.label: Publish Readiness
lanes.importStrategy: Reuse the local-vs-remote gate distinction for GitHub shipment messaging.
lanes.value: Prevents local progress from being mistaken for remote publication.
lanes.nextAction: Add remote readiness only after an origin is configured.

lanes.label: Full Next.js Import
lanes.importStrategy: Do not import wholesale. Extract only stable contracts and small UI patterns.
lanes.value: Could eventually provide richer app routes, but would change the repo's lightweight baseline.
lanes.nextAction: Keep blocked until dependency and deployment budgets are explicitly accepted.

readinessModel.label: Source is clean
readinessModel.definition: Candidate comes from source or docs, not generated cache, dependency folders, or runtime logs.

readinessModel.label: Contract first
readinessModel.definition: Candidate can be represented as JSON data, API output, or a documented checklist before runtime complexity.

readinessModel.label: UX value
readinessModel.definition: Candidate improves comprehension, task flow, accessibility, or product maturity.

readinessModel.label: Rollback simple
readinessModel.definition: Candidate can be removed in one small commit without breaking the root static baseline.
